translationRepairs: His father Fu had passed the jinshi examination in 1801; starting as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy, he rose to vice minister of rites, was honored with a second senior graduates' banquet, and was made junior guardian of the heir apparent. When he died he was posthumously ennobled as grand tutor and given the posthumous name Wenduan.

His father E had passed the jinshi examination in 1801; starting as a compiler in the Hanlin Academy, he rose to vice minister of rites, was honored with a second senior graduates' banquet, and was made junior guardian of the heir apparent. When he died he was posthumously ennobled as grand tutor and given the posthumous name Wenduan.
Chinese 堮 is Du E, not Fu; the English personal name is a mistransliteration.

His father Fu was a jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing; from Hanlin compiler he rose in succession to Vice Minister of Rites, was granted a second Deer-Ming banquet, appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and upon death was posthumously given Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenduan.

His father E was a jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing; from Hanlin compiler he rose in succession to Vice Minister of Rites, was granted a second Deer-Ming banquet, appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and upon death was posthumously given Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenduan.
Chinese 堮 is Du E, not Fu; the literal English personal name is a mistransliteration.

Xianfeng was stricken: he posthumously made Shoutian grand tutor and grand secretary, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, gave five thousand taels for the funeral, sent a close minister to console his father Fu, promoted his son Han from reviewer to chamberlain of the heir apparent, and granted all three grandsons the juren degree.

Chinese 堮 is Du E; English Fu is a mistransliteration carried from s0002.

Wenzong was deeply grieved; he posthumously granted Grand Tutor and Grand Secretary, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, granted five thousand taels for the funeral, sent a close official to comfort his father Fu, promoted his son the compiler Han to chamberlain for the heir, and granted all three grandsons the status of provincial graduates.

下河 denotes the Lixiahe region north of the Yangzi, not generically 'the lower Yangzi'.
